name: Proteus Syndrome

criteria.description: Mosaic distribution of lesions with asymmetric and disproportionate overgrowth
Presence of cerebriform connective tissue nevi
Presence of specific tumors such as ovarian cystadenomas or parotid monomorphic adenomas
Identification of somatic activating mutation in AKT1 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of mosaic, asymmetric overgrowth plus cerebriform connective tissue nevus and/or disproportionate skeletal overgrowth
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for AKT1 mutation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.notes: Highly characteristic skin lesion with brain-like surface

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mosaic distribution of overgrowth affecting multiple tissues
pathognomonic.notes: Involves skin, bone, and connective tissue

common.notes: Spinal curvature due to asymmetric growth

occasional.notes: Due to venous malformations and hypercoagulability
Benign tumors seen in some female patients
Increased risk due to vascular anomalies
Seizures or developmental delay in some cases

rare.notes: Enlarged heart due to overgrowth or secondary effects

laboratory: Elevated D-dimer and coagulation abnormalities in some patients
imaging: Asymmetric bone overgrowth on X-ray and MRI
Soft tissue overgrowth and lipomas on MRI
Venous malformations on Doppler ultrasound or MRI
genetic: Somatic activating mutation in AKT1 gene (c.49G>A, p.Glu17Lys)
other: Histopathology of connective tissue nevi shows thickened collagen bundles
Biopsy of tumors confirms benign nature

distinguishingFeatures: Limb hypertrophy without cerebriform connective tissue nevi
Café-au-lait skin pigmentation with irregular borders
Fibrous dysplasia of bone without mosaic AKT1 mutation

redFlags: Rapid asymmetric overgrowth causing functional impairment
Development of deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism
Presence of cerebriform connective tissue nevus
references: Biesecker LG. The challenges of Proteus syndrome: diagnosis and management. Eur J Hum Genet. 2006.
Lindhurst MJ et al. A mosaic activating mutation in AKT1 associated with the Proteus syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2011.
Sapp JC et al. Proteus syndrome: diagnostic criteria, differential diagnosis, and patient evaluation. Am J Med Genet A. 2012.
